articles.title: California man pleads guilty to supporting ISIS after plotting attack on alleged IDF soldier
articles.body:
A California man pleaded guilty on Friday to attempting to provide material support to a designated terrorist organization after pledging allegiance to the Islamic State terrorist organization (ISIS) and plotting to kill a man he suspected to be an IDF soldier.
According to a criminal complaint against 34-year-old Ammaad Akhtar, between February 2025 and June 2025 Akhtar attempted to provide funds, weapons, and equipment to ISIS.
Starting in February 2025, Akhtar began communicating with what he believed to be a member of ISIS and discussed a desire to travel overseas to fight with ISIS, ownership of multiple firearms, plans to attack a man he believed to be an IDF soldier, and a plan to commit a terrorist attack using homemade explosives.
Akhtar was actually communicating with an FBI Controlled Persona, which is a fake identity created and maintained by FBI agents for investigative purposes.
Akhtar glorified violent jihad, prayed to destroy infidels
Throughout Akhtar’s months-long communications with the persona, he repeatedly glorified jihad, expressed admiration for ISIS terrorists, stated that he wished to join the terrorist group, and said that he prayed to find ways to destroy those who do not believe in Islam.
“A lot of Muslims in America are too scared to talk about jihad,” Akhtar told the persona on March 13, 2025. “I don’t like being around them too much because they don’t ever want to form a group to go and beat up the kafir (infidels).”
Akhtar also owned three firearms and a knife, which he sent pictures of to the persona. He told the persona that he regularly carried the knife and a gun on his person so he could be ready in case he ever engaged in “conflict” with a non-believer.
In April, 2025, Akhtar began discussing plans to attack a Jewish man he believed to be an IDF soldier.
On April 3, he told the persona that he had driven by a synagogue and noticed a man he had previously seen around the synagogue on Saturdays.
Akhtar stated that he followed the man to find out where the man lives and asked the persona what he could do to “handle” the Jewish man once he located the home.
He told the persona that there is a lot of crime in his area and that he was thinking of killing the Jewish man in a place where it would seem like a random attack.
According to the criminal complaint, further FBI investigation into the synagogue indicated that the Jewish man does not appear to be an IDF soldier.
Akhtar started planning terrorist attack before being arrested
In May 2025, Akhtar shared that he had started making plans to carry out a terrorist attack at a populated event. He said he planned to infiltrate an event run by non-believers by dressing like them and pretending to be one of them, but told the persona he “needs some help in how to make a boom,” and accompanied the message with an explosion emoji.
He asked the persona for information on how to make an explosive device and stated that he had not yet chosen a target for the attack but would figure one out.
On June 23, 2025, Akhtar met in person with an undercover FBI agent he believed to be affiliated with ISIS. During the meeting, Akhtar gave the agent binoculars, $400 cash, two loaded guns, and six magazines of ammunition.
Akhtar was detained the next day and charged with attempting to provide material support to a designated foreign terrorist organization, which he pleaded guilty to on Friday.
He is scheduled to be sentenced in February 2027 and faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison with a $250,000 fine.

articles.title: US midterm early voting shatters record
articles.body:
US midterm early voting shatters record
More than 51 million Americans have cast ballots ahead of the US midterm elections, surpassing the previous early voting record set in 2022.
The November 3 elections, held halfway through a president’s four-year term, will determine control of Congress, with all 435 House seats and roughly a third of the Senate at stake. Republicans currently hold majorities in both chambers.
By Saturday, early voting had surpassed 51.3 million ballots, well above the previous record of 45.9 million set in 2022, according to data from the University of Florida Election Lab.
Across 27 states that track voters’ party registration, Democrats accounted for 43.1% of early ballots, compared with 31.8% for Republicans. The figures reflect voters’ party affiliations rather than their choices of candidates.
Pennsylvania recorded one of the widest gaps, with registered Democrats accounting for 65% of early ballots, compared with 25% for Republicans. In traditionally Republican Iowa, Kansas, and Nebraska, Democrats were nearly matching or exceeding GOP early turnout despite being outnumbered among registered voters.
Florida, Michigan, and Texas showed signs of renewed Republican participation in early and absentee voting. In Florida, Republicans had overtaken Democrats by three percentage points, compared with a 6.4-point advantage in 2022.
In Texas, Republicans accounted for 45% of early voters despite making up only 36% of the electorate, according to voter data firm L2. Its figures for Michigan showed that 30% of registered Republicans had voted early, compared with 23% of Democrats.
The Cook Political Report shifted its ratings for 12 House contests toward Democrats on Friday. The forecaster classified 18 House races and seven Senate contests as toss-ups.
“We know that early voters are going to be more Democratic. That’s been a feature of elections for a while now,” University of Florida Election Lab director Michael McDonald told Bloomberg.
“On Election Day the electorate shifts very much in the red direction. So Democrats have to build up an advantage in the early vote just to withstand what’s going to happen on Election Day,” he added.
Early voting was once a bipartisan practice, but voting patterns shifted during the Covid-19 pandemic. While many Democrats opted to vote by mail as a precaution in 2020, Republicans favored casting ballots in person on Election Day. That trend is now beginning to reverse, according to TargetSmart senior adviser Tom Bonier, cited by Bloomberg.
Trump has blamed mail-in voting for his 2020 defeat to Joe Biden, alleging widespread electoral fraud. In March, he signed an executive order directing the US Postal Service to introduce new requirements for handling mail ballots, including voter lists and tracking measures. On September 14, the Supreme Court declined to lift a lower court injunction blocking the Postal Service from enforcing the new rules ahead of the midterms. The president has softened his stance in recent weeks, urging supporters to vote early or by mail if they prefer.
The elections come amid low approval ratings for Trump, against the backdrop of the unpopular war in Iran and his administration’s aggressive immigration crackdown.
Trump is scheduled to hold rallies in Iowa and Kansas on Sunday after initially canceling the trips. The appearances were rearranged to accommodate additional tele-rallies, AP reported, citing a person familiar with the plans.

articles.title: 6.1-magnitude earthquake strikes off Japan's Mie Prefecture: JMA
articles.body:
TOKYO, Nov. 1 (Xinhua) -- An earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 6.1 struck off the southeast coast of Mie Prefecture, central Japan, on Sunday morning, the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) said.
According to the weather agency, the temblor occurred at around 7:15 a.m. local time at a depth of about 350 km, measuring 3 on Japan's 0-to-7 seismic-intensity scale in parts of Fukushima Prefecture.
The quake's epicenter was located at a latitude of 33.7 degrees north and a longitude of 137.1 degrees east.
No tsunami warning has been issued. ■

articles.body:
French police officers set ablaze amid unrest (VIDEOS)
Rioters hurled incendiary devices at police in Paris as another wave of cost-of-living protests swept across France on Saturday.
Five law enforcement officers were injured, including three by Molotov cocktails, according to police.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez described the attacks as “attempted murder.”
Videos from the scene show a Molotov cocktail being thrown at officers standing in formation with riot shields. One officer catches fire and is quickly engulfed in flames before a colleague uses a fire extinguisher to put out the blaze.

“The burning sensation is immediate, intense and grows stronger over time,” an unnamed gendarme injured by an incendiary device told BFMTV. “I couldn’t see it because you can’t look everywhere at once, and the barrage of projectiles was relentless,” he added.

Around 320,000 people rallied across France on Saturday, including 70,000 in Paris, according to the Interior Ministry. Organizers put the turnout at 500,000 nationwide, including 200,000 in the capital. Police said 565 people were arrested.
Paris authorities imposed a partial overnight curfew from 11pm to 6am in the areas around Place de la Republique, Place du Chatelet and Les Halles on Saturday and Sunday nights.
Although many demonstrations began peacefully, “radical elements” instigated riots in several cities, according to police. Nunez said there had been “calls for people to gather at 8pm to take advantage of Halloween night, wear masks and engage in looting, vandalism or attacks on public buildings.”
French media also reported incidents of alleged police brutality, with Le Monde describing officers striking apparently non-threatening protesters in Paris and two young men reportedly injured during arrests in Grenoble.
The protests began in September with high school students demanding better educational facilities, more teachers and increased funding. Separately, trade unions and Yellow Vest activists mobilized against rising living costs and fuel prices. The movements converged on October 17, bringing students, workers and other protesters together in nationwide demonstrations that have since broadened to include demands for civil liberties and an end to police violence.

articles.title: FBI accuses North Korea of hacking Binance crypto exchange
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, November 1. /TASS/. The US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has accused the North Korean authorities of a massive hacker attack on the Binance cryptocurrency exchange that could have led to losses of $6.3 bln, the FBI press service said.
The FBI said that North Korea is responsible for the theft of virtual assets worth over $6 bln from the Binance cryptocurrency exchange committed on or about October 29, 2026. The statement provides no evidence. US authorities believe the attack was organized by the TraderTraitor hacker group from North Korea. According to the FBI, the hackers will convert the stolen assets primarily into the Ethereum cryptocurrency. "It is expected these assets will then be further laundered by converting them using DeFi and instant swap services as they prepare them for further laundering stages," the bureau said.
The Binance cryptocurrency exchange will allocate 50% of the funds from its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to compensate for the losses caused by the hacker attack. The platform said earlier that it reimbursed 90% of the amount stolen during the attack.

articles.title: Brazil attracts 7 million foreign tourists in Jan-Sep 2026
articles.body:
Brazil attracts 7 million foreign tourists in Jan-Sep 2026
Brazil has welcomed around 7 million foreign tourists since the start of 2026, whilse spending by international visitors exceeded 45.6 billion Brazilian reais (around US$8.66 billion) between January and September, an increase of 10 per cent compared with the same period last year, TV BRICS reported.
According to the Brazilian Ministry of Tourism, citing data from the Central Bank, September alone saw record tourist spending of 4.9 billion Brazilian reais (approximately US$931 million).
The rise in tourist spending had a positive impact on the hotel, restaurant and tourism services sectors, as well as small businesses, coinciding with growth in international air traffic. The number of passengers on international flights reached 22.7 million during the first nine months of the year, an increase of 7.2 per cent year-on-year.
Business tourism contributed to the sector’s strong performance, generating revenue of 11.07 billion Brazilian reais (approximately US$2.1 billion) between January and September 2026, a rise of 7.41 per cent compared with the same period last year.
The impact of growth in tourism activity extended to the labour market, with the sector creating 62,000 formal jobs between August 2025 and August 2026. The total number of people employed in the sector rose to 2.42 million, representing around 5 per cent of the country’s workforce.
In a move aimed at attracting more visitors and boosting regional tourism, Brazil, in collaboration with Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay, launched a joint tourism portal, which was unveiled on 27 October 2026 during a meeting of tourism ministers from the Southern Common Market (Mercosur), hosted by the Uruguayan capital, Montevideo. The new platform allows travellers to explore tourist destinations according to their interests and to plan multi-country itineraries.

articles.title: Salvadoran families demand fair trials, mourn prison dead on Day of the Dead
articles.body:
By Wilfredo Pineda
SAN SALVADOR, Oct 31 (Reuters) - Relatives of people detained under El Salvador’s controversial state of exception gathered at the San Salvador metropolitan cathedral on Saturday to leave offerings for inmates who have died behind bars, demanding justice.
Participants arrived carrying yellow and red flowers, banners and photographs of jailed family members. Inside the capital’s cathedral, they knelt in prayer around the tomb of Archbishop Oscar Arnulfo Romero, a saint, and placed flowers there.
On the cathedral steps, the group held a rally honoring the dead and remembering relatives still in custody. Many of those present have had no contact with their detained relatives since their arrest, and - in some cases - do not know whether their relatives are still alive.
Natalia Funes, 61, a farmer from Puerto El Triunfo in the eastern province of Usulutan, attended in hopes of seeking answers about her jailed son. Her son, Oscar Orlando Rodriguez, was arrested in July 2022 and has been held incommunicado since.
“I am a distraught mother, a mother who has never seen my son. I am a mother who has never seen their face or heard from them,” Funes said.
El Salvador’s state of exception, imposed by President Nayib Bukele four years ago, has allowed security forces to detain more than 90,000 people.
Cristosal, a prominent human rights organization, has documented 454 deaths in Salvadoran prisons among people detained under the state of exception.
Many relatives of those still detained fear their loved ones will become an unwanted addition to the statistic.
Protesters used the Day of the Dead, observed on November 1 and 2 across several Latin American countries, to remember those who died behind bars, and also called for fair trials for detainees who remain jailed.
Liliana Urias, 44, spokeswoman for the Mothers for Freedom movement, said some members of the movement had lost a son, a brother or the father of their children.
“We are here in memory of all the innocent people who have died under the state of exception,” Urias said.
(Reporting by Wilfredo Pineda and Rodolfo Peña, Writing by Iñigo Alexander, Editing by Franklin Paul)
